_what: The size of one request at the door for people and AIs (src/mcp.rs `request_bytes`, read by every place that takes a request in on its way to the door). `request_bytes` is the one limit: the most bytes one door request may carry, its JSON-RPC message or HTTP body, whatever road it comes by (the local MCP route, the forwarder's public ingress, an HTTP request the forwarder carries to a computer under /a/<address>). It is 1 MiB for the records a records:write carries (the record contract's 1 MiB remote record bound, src/storage/record_store/README.md, and old trillion's door body bound, Trillion-X/trillion src/worker.mjs:761 `readBoundedJson(request.clone(), 1_000_000)`) plus `call_bytes` for the call around them (its JSON-RPC envelope, resource, operation, request key and other fields). A request larger than it is refused with 413 and the words `too_large`, which name the limit in bytes, so a caller's client tool knows to send its records in smaller writes; nothing larger is cut or dropped silently. One request crosses the session between the forwarder and a computer as one message, base64 inside JSON: such a message may be `request_bytes` in base64 (4/3 as long, rounded up to whole groups of 4) plus `call_bytes` for its envelope (src/mcp.rs `carried_message_bytes`). Answers are not bounded here: a door answer still fits one 64 KiB MCP message and pages past it (src/mcp.rs MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, `tool_answer_fits`).
request_key_why: The longest request key the door takes, in bytes. The industry floor is Stripe's: idempotency keys are up to 255 characters long (docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests, read 2026-11-12, "Idempotency keys are up to 255 characters long"). This door's key is stored as the TEXT primary key of eeaf_rust_receipts (src/eeaf_store.rs:852), which has no length bound of its own, so no storage limit is larger than this one. The earlier value of 512 had no recorded basis (commit 860eea39b). A key over this bound is refused before anything runs, naming its length.
